subtitle: In Nalanda’s Hall of Judgment, a Silent Monk Finds His Voice

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Shantideva stepping toward an ornate lion-shaped seat before shadowed monks in a vast Nalanda hall
panels.action: Śāntideva walks calmly toward a carved lion throne at the center of a stone-pillared Nalanda assembly hall, robed monks watching from shadowed tiers.

dialogue.text: At Nalanda, c. 8th century, they mocked Śāntideva as lazy. Tradition says he answered by taking the lion seat and giving India one of its deepest works of courage and compassion.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी के नालंदा में, शांतिदेव को आलसी कहकर चिढ़ाया जाता था। परंपरा कहती है, वे सिंहासन पर बैठे और भारत को साहस और करुणा की गहरी रचना दे गए।

panels.shot: epic aerial over Nalanda’s sprawling brick monasteries and stupas under a hazy Magadhan sky
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view reveals Nalanda’s red-brick monasteries, tall gateways and courtyards crowded with robed scholars, smoke rising from kitchens under the pale sky of Magadha.

dialogue.text: Nalanda, in Magadha, was a city of scholars. Thousands of monks studied logic, grammar, medicine, and the vast philosophies of the Buddha in its brick halls.

i18n.hi: मगध का नालंदा विद्वानों का नगर था। हज़ारों भिक्षु ईंटों की वीथिकाओं में तर्क, व्याकरण, आयुर्वेद और बुद्ध की विशाल दार्शनिक धाराएँ पढ़ते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in through a cloistered corridor lined with monks debating, scribes copying palm-leaf manuscripts
panels.action: Inside a vaulted corridor, senior monks debate with raised hands while younger scribes sit cross-legged, copying palm-leaf manuscripts by lamplight onto neat black-script lines.

dialogue.text: Here, brilliance was tested in public. Students recited from memory, defended arguments, and were judged by their peers and elders in formal assemblies.

i18n.hi: यहाँ प्रतिभा खुले आम कसौटी पर चढ़ती थी। छात्र कंठस्थ बोलते, तर्क साधते और औपचारिक सभाओं में साथियों व गुरुओं से परखे जाते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shantideva alone in a quiet cell, sitting in meditation beside neatly stacked manuscripts
panels.action: Śāntideva sits on a simple mat in a small brick cell, eyes half-closed in meditation, palm-leaf bundles stacked beside him, a single shaft of light cutting through the dim.

dialogue.text: Śāntideva enters this world as a quiet monk. Sources remember him more through his works than his life: a thinker immersed in the path of the bodhisattva.

i18n.hi: शांतिदेव इस जगत में एक शांत भिक्षु की तरह प्रवेश करते हैं। उन्हें जीवन से कम, ग्रंथों से ज़्यादा याद किया जाता है—बोधिसत्व मार्ग में डूबा हुआ मननशील साधक।

panels.shot: wide shot of the monastic refectory where monks eat and Śāntideva is absent, others glancing and whispering
panels.action: In a crowded refectory, lines of monks eat from simple bowls; an empty space where Śāntideva should sit draws sidelong glances and hushed whispers among the younger monks.

dialogue.text: Later Tibetan and Sanskrit biographies tell a sharp story: monks saw Śāntideva as idle, skipping communal duties and avoiding public debates.

i18n.hi: बाद के तिब्बती और संस्कृत जीवन-वृत्तांत एक तीखी कथा कहते हैं: भिक्षु शांतिदेव को निकम्मा समझते, सामूहिक काम टालते और सार्वजनिक वाद-विवाद से दूर भागते देखते।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of Shantideva walking calmly past a group of monks who gossip in the cloister
panels.action: Śāntideva walks slowly along a cloister, gaze lowered and unreadable, while a knot of monks watch him pass and murmur, some smirking, some frowning.

dialogue.text: They nicknamed him ‘the three things’: eating, sleeping, and wandering. In a community that prized loud learning, his silence looked like failure.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने नाम रखा ‘तीन काम’—खाना, सोना और घूमना। जहाँ ऊँची आवाज़ में विद्या का मान था, वहाँ उसका मौन निकृष्ट लगने लगा।

panels.shot: interior wide of the main hall, senior monks seated in rows as one gestures toward an ornate lion seat platform
panels.action: In Nalanda’s main assembly hall, senior monks sit in disciplined rows before a raised platform with a lion-shaped seat; one elder points at it while addressing the gathering.

dialogue.text: Biographical tradition says the monks set a test. Śāntideva must mount the lion seat and give a formal teaching, proving he deserved Nalanda’s robes.

i18n.hi: कथा कहती है, भिक्षुओं ने परीक्षा रखी। शांतिदेव को सिंहासन पर बैठकर औपचारिक उपदेश देना था, ताकि सिद्ध हो कि वे नालंदा के वस्त्र के योग्य हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot as Shantideva is summoned by attendants toward the hall, his face calm, hands folded around a manuscript
panels.action: Two attendants gesture for Śāntideva to follow; he walks toward the hall, calm and steady, one hand lightly resting on a wrapped palm-leaf manuscript at his side.

dialogue.speaker: shantideva
dialogue.text: If you wish me to teach, I will speak of the bodhisattva’s way.

i18n.hi: यदि आप चाहते हैं कि मैं सिखाऊँ, तो मैं बोधिसत्व मार्ग पर बोलूँगा।

panels.shot: sweeping interior wide as Shantideva climbs steps to the lion seat before packed tiers of monks
panels.action: Śāntideva ascends the stone steps to the lion seat, his saffron robe flowing around him; tiers of monks watch, some amused, some curious, the vast hall hushed.

dialogue.text: He takes the lion seat. The gathered community expects a stumbling novice. Instead, tradition says, they hear a work that will echo far beyond Nalanda.

i18n.hi: वह सिंहासन पर बैठता है। सभा को लगता है, कोई घबराया नवदीक्षित लड़खड़ाएगा। पर परंपरा कहती है, वहाँ से ऐसी ध्वनि उठती है जो नालंदा से बहुत दूर तक गूँजती है।

panels.shot: tight three-quarter view of Shantideva seated cross-legged on the lion seat, eyes lowered, beginning to recite
panels.action: Śāntideva sits cross-legged on the lion throne, eyes lowered in concentration, right hand raised in a gentle teaching gesture as his lips form measured Sanskrit syllables.

dialogue.text: He begins: the Bodhicaryavatara, ‘Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva’. A long, structured poem on how to live for the awakening of all beings.

i18n.hi: वह आरंभ करता है ‘बोधिचर्यावतार’—बोधिसत्व के पथ में प्रवेश। यह दीर्घ, क्रमबद्ध काव्य है, जो सभी प्राणियों के जागरण के लिए जीने की साधना बताता है।

panels.shot: montage-style wide with faint overlays of verses as monks listen, some leaning forward, expressions softening
panels.action: Monks lean forward, faces intent, as Śāntideva’s steady recitation fills the hall; the visual hints of poetic meter and verse flow between speaker and audience.

dialogue.text: Chapter after chapter, he sings of generosity, ethics, patience, vigor, meditation and wisdom—using verse to bind philosophy to daily effort and feeling.

i18n.hi: अध्याय पर अध्याय, वह दान,शील, क्षमा, वीर्य, ध्यान और प्रज्ञा का गान करता है—कविता से दर्शन को रोज़मर्रा के प्रयास और भावना से जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: medium shot from behind Shantideva, facing rows of monks, as he gestures in emphasis for the compassion chapters
panels.action: From behind Śāntideva we see his hand sweep outward toward the monks as he recites, their faces reflecting awe and unease at the depth of compassion he describes.

dialogue.speaker: shantideva
dialogue.text: May I be a boat, a bridge, a road for all beings who seek the farther shore.

i18n.hi: मैं उन सब के लिए नौका, पुल, पथ बनूँ जो पार की ओर बढ़ना चाहते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on Shantideva’s intense, serene profile as he enters the ninth chapter, fingers marking points in the air
panels.action: A close view shows Śāntideva’s face sharpened with focus, one finger subtly tracing points in the air as he debates an unseen opponent through his words.

dialogue.text: Then comes chapter nine. The voice turns analytical, testing concepts of self and things with Madhyamaka reasoning, arguing that clinging to fixed essence breaks compassion.

i18n.hi: फिर आता है नवाँ अध्याय। स्वर विश्लेषी हो जाता है—माध्यमक तर्क से आत्मा और वस्तुओं की धारणाओं को परखते हुए दिखाता है कि किसी स्थायी सार से चिपटना करुणा को तोड़ देता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the hall, some monks frowning, others excited, as they grapple with the logical arguments unfolding
panels.action: Across the hall, some monks furrow their brows in intense thought, others sit upright with sudden clarity, as Śāntideva’s argument on emptiness unfolds like a careful debate.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars note: this is not mere piety. It is a rigorous philosophical debate, using logic to show how wisdom and compassion arise together.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान कहते हैं: यह केवल भक्ति नहीं। यह कठोर दार्शनिक वाद है, जो तर्क से दिखाता है कि प्रज्ञा और करुणा साथ-साथ कैसे जन्म लेते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot as a scribe monk begins hurriedly to write, listening raptly to Shantideva’s verses
panels.action: Near the front, a young monk pulls out palm leaves and stylus, bending close as he starts to scratch down verses while listening, sweat beading at his brow.

dialogue.text: The biographies say scribes rushed to write as he spoke. Whether or not every detail is exact, the text itself survives, carrying Nalanda’s voice into later centuries.

i18n.hi: जीवन-वृत्त कहते हैं, लेखक तत्क्षण लिखने दौड़े। हर बात ठीक हो या न हो, स्वयं ग्रंथ बचा रहा, नालंदा की वाणी को आगे के युगों में ढोता हुआ।

panels.shot: close-up on a palm-leaf manuscript of Bodhicaryavatara being carefully tied and stored in Nalanda’s library
panels.action: Hands of a librarian monk gently stack and tie palm-leaf folios etched with the Bodhicaryavatara’s opening lines, placing them among other texts in Nalanda’s dim library.

dialogue.text: Śāntideva also composes the Śikṣāsamuccaya, a vast anthology on training. Both works show how Nalanda linked ethical practice, textual learning, and subtle reasoning.

i18n.hi: शांतिदेव का ‘शिक्षासमुच्चय’ भी है—अभ्यास पर विशाल संकलन। दोनों ग्रंथ दिखाते हैं कि नालंदा ने आचरण, शास्त्र और सूक्ष्म तर्क को कैसे एक सूत्र में बाँधा।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide as centuries pass: Nalanda’s bricks weather, while the manuscript travels with monks along trade routes
panels.action: The bricks of Nalanda fade under time, while overlaid scenes show monks carrying wrapped manuscripts along forest paths and caravan roads toward the Himalayas and beyond.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, the Bodhicaryavatara is studied in Tibetan monasteries, translated and commented on, its Nalanda-born verses shaping Mahayana thought far from Magadha.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद भी तिब्बती मठों में ‘बोधिचर्यावतार’ पढ़ा, अनूदित और व्याख्यायित होता है; मगध से दूर तक महायान चिंतन उसकी नालंदा-जन्मी पंक्तियों से ढलता है।

panels.shot: modern-era interior of a study with the Bodhicaryavatara open in Sanskrit and translation, a reader’s hand resting thoughtfully on the page
panels.action: A modern desk holds the Bodhicaryavatara open in Sanskrit, with a translated volume beside it; a reader’s hand rests near the margin, pausing mid-line in reflection.

dialogue.text: Today, scholars like Crosby, Skilton and Williams read Śāntideva as a key voice in Mahayana, probing how compassion, ethics and emptiness can guide a human life.

i18n.hi: आज क्रॉस्बी, स्किल्टन और विलियम्स जैसे विद्वान शांतिदेव को महायान की केंद्रीय वाणी मानते हैं—जाँचते हैं कि करुणा, नीति और शून्यता किसी मानव जीवन को कैसे दिशा दे सकती है।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of Shantideva back in his cell, seen in memory, sitting quietly as light falls on his face
panels.action: Śāntideva sits once more in his small cell, imagined in soft light, eyes peaceful, as if the noise of the hall has fallen away and only the inner work remains.

dialogue.text: The lion seat story is legend, but the texts are real. Nalanda’s ‘idle’ monk left a disciplined path that still asks: what work are we doing in silence, ready to speak when called?

i18n.hi: सिंहासन की कथा चाहे दंतकथा हो, पर ग्रंथ वास्तविक हैं। नालंदा का ‘निकम्मा’ भिक्षु एक अनुशासित पथ छोड़ गया जो आज भी पूछता है: हम मौन में कौन सा काम साध रहे हैं, जो पुकार पड़ते ही बोल उठेगा?

subtitle_i18n.en: In Nalanda’s Hall of Judgment, a Silent Monk Finds His Voice
subtitle_i18n.hi: नालंदा के न्याय सभागार में, मौन भिक्षु को मिलती है आवाज़
